title: A wedding in India
scene: Anna's friend from college invites her to a wedding in India. The women wear saris, the men wear dhotis and turbans, a Sikh uncle tells stories about an old raja and a British sahib, a snake charmer shows a cobra, and at a temple puja a mystic reads Sanskrit and gives everyone prasad.

words.ex: She wore a beautiful red sari to the wedding.
He wore a white dhoti for the festival.
He wears a turban to work every day.
Many Sikhs wear a turban as part of their faith.
The raja lived in a huge palace.
In the old story, the servant called him sahib.
The cobra raised its head and hissed.
The family does a puja every morning.
The old mystic spent years in prayer.
Sanskrit is an ancient language of India.
After the prayer, we received prasad.
The maharaja lived in a beautiful palace.

old_story: Anna's college friend Priya invited her to a wedding in India. All the women wore bright [[saris|sari]], and Anna wore a borrowed one too. Priya's grandfather wore a white [[dhoti]], and her uncle wore a red [[turban]]. The uncle is a [[Sikh]], and he loves telling old stories. He told Anna about a rich [[raja]] who lived in a golden palace. In the story, a foreign visitor made the servants call him [[sahib]]. After lunch, a snake charmer showed the guests a [[cobra]] in a basket. In the evening, the family went to the temple for a [[puja]]. An old [[mystic]] read prayers in [[Sanskrit]] with his eyes closed. At the end, he gave everyone sweet [[prasad]]. Anna said it was the most beautiful day of her year.

title: Istanbul, Dubai and Cairo
scene: Max's parents travel around the Middle East. In Istanbul they shop in a bazaar, pay in lira and hear about a pasha who ruled the city; in Dubai they meet a sheikh in his emirate and pay in dinars on the way; they ride to an oasis, see a mirage and a scorpion, and in Egypt they hear a mullah, see the Sphinx and the Nile delta.

words.ex: We bought spices and carpets at the bazaar.
The sheikh welcomed the guests to his palace.
Dubai is one of the seven emirates.
The travelers stopped at an oasis in the desert.
The lake in the desert was just a mirage.
A scorpion was hiding in my shoe this morning.
We saw the Great Sphinx in Egypt.
The emir welcomed the foreign guests.

old_story: Max's parents took a long trip around the Middle East this spring. In Istanbul, they went shopping in an old [[bazaar]]. Max's mom paid two hundred [[lira]] for a small blue [[amulet]] for Max. A guide told them about a [[pasha]] who ruled the city long ago. In Dubai, they visited a palace where a [[sheikh]] once welcomed guests. The guide explained that Dubai is the biggest city of its [[emirate]]. On a short stop in Jordan, they paid for a taxi in [[dinars|dinar]]. Then they rode camels across the desert to a green [[oasis]]. On the way, Max's dad saw a lake, but it was only a [[mirage]]. In the morning, a [[scorpion]] was sleeping in his shoe! In Cairo, they heard a [[mullah]] lead the morning prayers at an old mosque. They saw the Great [[Sphinx|sphinx]] and took a boat trip to the Nile [[delta]].

title: Dad's small bakery
scene: Anna's dad becomes a businessman: he opens a small bakery with a business partner. They write a business plan, check the cash flow and the profit, decide on their pricing, choose a vendor for flour, talk to a retailer about retail, hire a sales manager, join a farmers' cooperative and sometimes use barter.

words.ex: My uncle is a successful businessman in Kyiv.
My business partner and I opened a cafe together.
She wrote a business plan for her new bakery.
The company has a cash flow problem.
The shop made a small profit this year.
Our pricing is simple and clear.
We chose a new software vendor this year.
This retailer sells clothes online and in stores.
My sister has worked in retail for five years.
The sales manager wants better numbers this month.
The farmers in our village formed a cooperative.
They used barter instead of money.
The company is the main distributor in the region.
My aunt is a successful businesswoman.
I bought my car from a local dealer.

old_story: Last year, Anna's dad decided to become a [[businessman]]. He opened a small bakery with his old friend Taras, who became his [[business partner]]. First, they wrote a [[business plan]], and Anna helped them check the [[cash flow]] every week. After six months, the bakery made its first small [[profit]]. They kept their [[pricing]] simple: every pie cost the same. They chose a local [[vendor]] for flour and sugar. Soon a big [[retailer]] wanted to sell their bread in its stores. Taras had worked in [[retail]] before, so he knew what to say. Then they hired a [[sales manager]] named Iryna. They also joined a farmers' [[cooperative]] to get fresh milk and eggs. Sometimes they even used [[barter]] and paid the farmers with fresh bread. Now a regional [[distributor]] takes their pies to five towns.

title: Max's startup
scene: Max and two friends start their own startup. The founder explains the concept, the business model and a use case to an investor, who sees a game changer and a win-win deal; he offers venture capital for their know-how, they get a patent, and later they plan a joint venture and a spin-off.

words.ex: She works at a tech startup.
I met the founder of the company at a conference.
I really like the concept of this new cafe.
Their business model is based on monthly subscriptions.
Can you give me a simple use case for this app?
We need an investor for our small business.
This new phone app is a real game changer for small shops.
This deal is a win-win situation for both companies.
Their new business venture is doing very well.
They need more capital to start the business.
She has the know-how to fix old cars.
She got a patent for her invention.
He was a great innovator in medicine.
The two companies started a joint venture in Poland.

old_story: Max and two friends started their own [[startup]] last spring. As the [[founder]], Max had to explain the idea to everyone. The [[concept]] was simple: an app that plans cheap, healthy meals for students. Their [[business model]] was a small monthly payment. Max showed a simple [[use case]]: a tired student opens the app and finds dinner. An [[investor]] named Mrs. Bondar listened carefully. She said the app could be a [[game changer]] for busy students. She offered them a [[win-win]] deal and asked to join their [[venture]]. She put in the [[capital]], and the team brought their [[know-how]]. Soon they got a [[patent]] for their smart shopping list. A local newspaper called Max a young [[innovator]]. His mom cut out the article and put it on the fridge.

title: Anna's marketing seminar
scene: At a marketing seminar Anna studies a case study about branding. She creates a logo and a slogan with an art director, plans targeting for the mass market, reads what the respondents said, compares the results with a benchmark, and learns about merchandising, promotion and gift vouchers.

words.ex: My sister works in marketing at a big company.
I have a seminar on marketing tomorrow.
We discussed a case study in today's marketing class.
Good branding helps a company stand out.
The company changed its logo last year.
The company needs a catchy new slogan.
The art director chose the colors for the ad.
Better targeting helps ads reach the right people.
The product is made for the mass market.
Most respondents said they liked the new design.
The new phone scored high on the benchmark.
The store has a special promotion this week.
Our landing page shows the price and a sign-up button.
I signed up for a free writing workshop.
She gave a talk at a medical symposium last month.
Our shop uses email marketing to tell customers about sales.

old_story: Anna is studying [[marketing]], and on Friday she went to a [[seminar]] at her university. The teacher gave the class a [[case study]] about a small juice company. The company had good juice but very weak [[branding]]. A real [[art director]] helped Anna's team create a new [[logo]] and a [[slogan]]. Then they talked about [[targeting]]: who should buy this juice? Anna's team wanted to sell it to the [[mass market]], not only to rich people. They read a survey, and most [[respondents|respondent]] liked the green bottles. They compared their sales numbers with a [[benchmark]] from a bigger company. Next, they learned about [[merchandising]] and where to put bottles in a store. Anna suggested a summer [[promotion]]: buy two bottles, get one free. Finally, they designed a simple [[landing page]] with the price and a big orange button. The teacher said their project was the best in the class.
